verdict.rationale: SES documents a getting-started path: verify an email address or domain, then send by SDK, SMTP or API. It openly states the sandbox restriction that you can only send to verified identities, so required setup is surfaced rather than hidden. Nothing in the pack shows a copy-paste, language-specific quickstart or a signup-to-delivery time measured in minutes. missing for 10: copy-paste complete per-language quickstart code, evidence of minutes-to-first-email, independent hands-on corroboration of the onboarding flow.

support.subject: As a developer, I can go from signup to my first delivered email in minutes — the quickstart is copy-paste complete for my language and doesn't hide required setup

citations.quote: Get started with SES by verifying an email address and sending domain so that you can start sending email through SES
When your account is in the sandbox, you can only send email to verified identities.
You can send email from Amazon EC2 by using an AWS SDK, by using the Amazon SES SMTP interface, or by making calls directly to the Amazon SES API.
